entities.summary:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP, भारतीय जनता पार्टी, meaning 'Indian People's Party'), founded in 1980 from the ruins of the Janata Party — is India's dominant right-wing Hindu nationalist political party, currently the world's largest political party by membership (approximately 180 million members) and the governing party of India under Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014. The BJP represents the political expression of Hindu nationalism (Hindutva ideology) developed by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) organizational ecosystem.

The BJP's ideological foundations trace to the RSS (founded 1925), the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP, 1964), and other organizations of the Sangh Parivar (family of RSS-affiliated organizations) that advocate for Hindu Rashtra (Hindu nation) as the vision for India. The BJP was the political wing of this broader Hindutva movement, though the party's mainstream positioning often softens the harder-edge Hindutva positions of affiliated organizations.

Narendra Modi's 2014 and 2019 election victories with large majorities represented a historic shift in Indian politics: BJP governments have pursued Hindu nationalist policies including the revocation of Jammu and Kashmir's special constitutional status (Article 370, 2019), the Citizenship Amendment Act (2019), and the Ram Temple construction at Ayodhya (consecrated 2024) on the disputed site of the demolished Babri Masjid. Critics argue India's secular democratic character is under threat; supporters argue these represent rightful assertions of Hindu cultural heritage. The BJP's period is one of Indian history's most consequential political transformations.
